cues.text: Spotted at six-a-side
Gareth Bale was born in 1989 in Cardiff, in Wales.
When he was nine, scouts from Southampton saw him playing six-a-side football for his first club, Cardiff Civil Service.
He was quick and loved to run with the ball.
Kick the ball.
Southampton invited him to train with them.
It was the start of a long journey.
He was still a schoolboy, and he trained with Southampton while he grew up.
Enjoy playing. Fun games are where great players begin.
Special rules
Gareth was so good at school football that his PE teacher, Gwyn Morris, gave him special rules.
He was only allowed one touch of the ball, and he was not allowed to use his left foot, his best foot.
That made the games fairer for the other children.
Tap the ball three times.
The rules made the game fair for everyone, and they made Gareth practise his other skills.
Making things harder for yourself is a great way to get better.
The youngest for Wales
In April 2006, when he was sixteen, Gareth played his first match for Southampton.
A few weeks later, he became the youngest player ever to play for Wales, at sixteen years and 315 days.
He played at left-back, running up and down the wing.
Flip the shirt.
In 2007, he moved to Tottenham Hotspur in London.
London was a big new city, and Tottenham was a big new club.
Young players can do big things when they are ready and given a chance.
The unlucky run
At Tottenham, something strange happened.
Gareth played in 24 Premier League games, and his team did not win any of them.
For two years, the run went on, and some people even called him unlucky.
It was not his fault, but people still talked about it.
Lift the rain cloud.
It is hard when people say you are unlucky.
Gareth kept training and kept playing his best.
A bad run is just a run. It does not say who you are.
The run is over
In September 2009, Gareth came on as a substitute near the end of a game against Burnley.
Tottenham won 5–0.
At last, the run was over!
His teammates were happy for him.
Flip the scoreboard.
Then his manager moved him from left-back to the wing, and Gareth became one of the most exciting players in the world.
In 2011 and 2013, the other players voted him their Player of the Year.
Sometimes a small change, like a new position, can help you shine.
A hero for Wales
In 2013, Real Madrid signed Gareth for a world-record fee, and he won the Champions League five times.
In 2016, he led Wales to the semi-finals of the European Championship.
He scored many important goals in big finals.
Raise the banner.
In 2022, he helped Wales reach the World Cup for the first time since 1958.
Gareth stopped playing in January 2023.
Unlucky moments pass. Keep working, and your luck can turn.
